+{{

+    )
+}}
+
+/*
+    customer_ltv: corrected customer lifetime value.
+
+    Fixes vs. dim_customers.lifetime_value:
+      1. Same order exists in both SAP and POS feeds. Orders are deduplicated
+         by order_id before summing, so revenue is not double counted.
+      2. Cancellations are detected from status text (case-insensitive,
+         e.g. 'CANCELLED' / 'cancelled' with no cancelled_at), the cancelled_at
+         timestamp and the is_cancelled flag. An order is excluded if any copy
+         of it is cancelled.
+*/
+
+with order_copies as (
+
+    select
+        order_id,
+        max(customer_id) as customer_id,
+        max(grand_total) as order_value,
+        min(cast(ordered_at as date)) as order_date,
+        max(
+            case
+                when upper(trim(status)) = 'CANCELLED'
+                  or cancelled_at is not null
+                  or is_cancelled
+                then 1
+                else 0
+            end
+        ) as is_cancelled_any
+    from {{ ref('int_sales__orders_enriched') }}
+    where order_id is not null
+    group by order_id
+
+),
+
+valid_orders as (
+
+    select
+        customer_id,
+        order_id,
+        order_value,
+        order_date
+    from order_copies
+    where is_cancelled_any = 0
+      and customer_id is not null
+
+),
+
+customer_metrics as (
+
+    select
+        customer_id,
+        count(distinct order_id) as total_orders,
+        sum(order_value) as lifetime_value,
+        avg(order_value) as avg_order_value,
+        min(order_date) as first_order_date,
+        max(order_date) as last_order_date
+    from valid_orders
+    group by customer_id
+
+),
+

+
+    select
+        c.customer_id,

+

+-- 1. fct_sales fans out (SAP header duplicates and POS mirrors), so keep one row per order_line_id.

+

+
+    select
+        order_line_id,
+        customer_id,
+        order_id,
+        order_date,
+        line_total,

+        ) as rn

+    where customer_id is not null
+
+),
+

+
+    select distinct order_id

+    where order_id is not null
+      and (

+      )
+
+),
+
+valid_lines as (
+
+    select l.*
+    from sales_lines l
+    where l.rn = 1
+      and not exists (

+        order_id,

+

+        sum(order_value) as lifetime_value,

+

+
+    select distinct customer_id

+

+    where customer_id is not null
+

+        cast(

+                     else 0 end,
+                2
+            ) as decimal(18, 2)
+        ) as avg_order_value,

diff --git a/models/marts/customer/customer_ltv.sql b/models/marts/customer/customer_ltv.sql
--- /dev/null
+++ b/models/marts/customer/customer_ltv.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,145 @@
+{{
+    config(
+        materialized='table',
+        tags=['mart', 'customers', 'ltv']
+    )
+}}
+
+/*
+================================================================================
+customer_ltv
+
+Corrected customer lifetime value. Replaces the overstated LTV that was
+previously derived from int_sales__orders_enriched / fct_sales.
+
+Why the previous numbers were overstated:
+  1. Orders present in both SAP and POS were counted twice (int_sales__orders_enriched
+     has 4,216 rows but only 2,664 distinct order_ids).
+  2. Cancelled orders were included (status 'CANCELLED', cancelled_at set, or
+     a row in ORDERS.ORDER_CANCELLATIONS).
+  3. Orders fully refunded via a REFUND return (COMPLETED / PROCESSED) were
+     included.
+  4. grand_total is in transaction currency (JPY, GBP, EUR, ...) and was summed
+     without conversion to USD.
+
+Valid order = one row per order_id that is neither cancelled nor refunded.
+Order value = grand_total / exchange_rate (USD), one copy per order.
+
+Status codes are abbreviated in the source ('C' = COMPLETED, 'D' = DELIVERED,
+'S' = SHIPPED, 'P' = PROCESSING/PENDING), so status is normalized with
+upper(trim()) and only 'CANCELLED' is treated as a cancellation.
+
+Unpaid / pending orders are NOT excluded here (judgment call: they are not yet
+cancelled or refunded). Revisit if Finance wants only paid orders counted.
+================================================================================
+*/
+
+with orders_raw as (
+
+    select
+        order_id,
+        customer_id,
+        -- grand_total is in transaction currency; exchange_rate is units of
+        -- transaction currency per 1 USD (e.g. JPY 149.5 per USD), so divide.
+        grand_total / nullif(exchange_rate, 0)             as grand_total_usd,
+        ordered_at,
+        upper(trim(status)) as order_status,
+        cancelled_at,
+        source_system
+    from {{ ref('int_sales__orders_enriched') }}
+    where order_id is not null
+
+),
+
+-- One row per order: SAP and POS can both carry the same order_id
+orders_dedup as (
+
+    select
+        order_id,
+        max(customer_id)                                   as customer_id,
+        round(max(grand_total_usd), 2)                     as order_value,
+        max(ordered_at)                                    as ordered_at,
+        bool_or(order_status = 'CANCELLED'
+                or cancelled_at is not null)               as is_cancelled_status
+    from orders_raw
+    group by order_id
+
+),
+
+cancelled_orders as (
+
+    select distinct order_id
+    from {{ source('orders', 'ORDER_CANCELLATIONS') }}
+    where order_id is not null
+
+),
+
+refunded_orders as (
+
+    select distinct order_id
+    from {{ source('orders', 'RETURNS') }}
+    where upper(trim(RETURN_TYPE)) = 'REFUND'
+      and upper(trim(STATUS)) in ('COMPLETED', 'PROCESSED')
+      and order_id is not null
+
+),
+
+valid_orders as (
+
+    select
+        o.order_id,
+        o.customer_id,
+        o.order_value,
+        cast(o.ordered_at as date) as order_date
+    from orders_dedup o
+    where o.customer_id is not null
+      and not o.is_cancelled_status
+      and o.order_id not in (select order_id from cancelled_orders)
+      and o.order_id not in (select order_id from refunded_orders)
+
+),
+
+customer_metrics as (
+
+    select
+        customer_id,
+        count(*)                                 as total_orders,
+        sum(order_value)                         as lifetime_value_raw,
+        avg(order_value)                         as avg_order_value_raw,
+        min(order_date)                          as first_order_date,
+        max(order_date)                          as last_order_date
+    from valid_orders
+    group by customer_id
+
+),
+
+final as (
+
+    select
+        c.customer_id,
+        cast(coalesce(m.total_orders, 0) as integer)                       as total_orders,
+        cast(round(coalesce(m.lifetime_value_raw, 0), 2) as decimal(18,2)) as lifetime_value,
+        cast(round(coalesce(m.avg_order_value_raw, 0), 2) as decimal(18,2)) as avg_order_value,
+        m.first_order_date,
+        m.last_order_date
+    from {{ ref('int_customers__unified') }} c
+    left join customer_metrics m
+        on c.customer_id = m.customer_id
+
+)
+
+select
+    customer_id,
+    total_orders,
+    lifetime_value,
+    avg_order_value,
+    first_order_date,
+    last_order_date,
+    case
+        when lifetime_value >= 1000 then 'VIP'
+        when lifetime_value >= 500  then 'High Value'
+        when lifetime_value >= 100  then 'Medium Value'
+        when lifetime_value > 0     then 'Low Value'
+        else 'No Value'
+    end as value_segment
+from final

+Corrected customer lifetime value. Only orders that produced actual, retained
+revenue for the company are summed.
+
+Excluded from LTV (an order is "valid" only if none of these apply):
+  - Cancelled: status = 'CANCELLED' or cancelled_at is set
+  - Returned: status = 'RETURNED' (full order returned, revenue reversed)
+  - Unpaid: payment_status <> 'PAID' (no money collected)
+  - Chargeback: chargeback_flag = 1 (payment reversed by the card network)
+  - Test / sample / internal orders, and exclude_from_reporting = true
+    (NULL flags are treated as false)
+
+The previous calculation (int_customers__lifetime_metrics, rpt_customer_
+lifetime_value_deciles) counted cancelled orders, unpaid orders and test /
+internal orders, which overstated LTV.
+
+Grain: one row per customer. Customers with no valid orders are kept with zeros
+and value_segment = 'No Value'.
+================================================================================
+*/
+
+with customers as (
+    select distinct customer_id
+    from {{ ref('stg_customer__customers') }}
+    where customer_id is not null
+),
+
+valid_orders as (
+    select
+        customer_id,
+        order_id,
+        cast(ordered_at as date) as order_date,
+        grand_total
+    from {{ ref('stg_orders__orders') }}
+    where customer_id is not null
+        and grand_total is not null
+        and status not in ('CANCELLED', 'RETURNED')
+        and cancelled_at is null
+        and payment_status = 'PAID'
+        and coalesce(chargeback_flag, 0) = 0
+        and coalesce(test_order_flag, false) = false
+        and coalesce(sample_order_flag, false) = false
+        and coalesce(internal_order_flag, false) = false
+        and coalesce(exclude_from_reporting, false) = false
+),
+
+order_agg as (
+    select
+        customer_id,
+        count(distinct order_id) as total_orders,
+        sum(grand_total) as lifetime_value,
+        avg(grand_total) as avg_order_value,
+        min(order_date) as first_order_date,
+        max(order_date) as last_order_date
+    from valid_orders
+    group by customer_id
+),
+
+-- Spine: every known customer, plus any customer with valid orders that is
+-- missing from the customer master, so no valid revenue is dropped.
+all_customers as (
+    select customer_id from customers
+    union
+    select customer_id from order_agg
+),
+
+final as (
+    select
+        c.customer_id,
+        coalesce(o.total_orders, 0) as total_orders,
+        round(coalesce(o.lifetime_value, 0), 2) as lifetime_value,
+        round(coalesce(o.avg_order_value, 0), 2) as avg_order_value,
+        o.first_order_date,
+        o.last_order_date
+    from all_customers c
+    left join order_agg o
+        on o.customer_id = c.customer_id
+)
+
+select
+    customer_id,
+    cast(total_orders as integer) as total_orders,
+    cast(lifetime_value as decimal(18, 2)) as lifetime_value,
+    cast(avg_order_value as decimal(18, 2)) as avg_order_value,
+    cast(first_order_date as date) as first_order_date,
+    cast(last_order_date as date) as last_order_date,
+    case
+        when lifetime_value is null or lifetime_value = 0 then 'No Value'
+        when lifetime_value >= 1000 then 'VIP'
+        when lifetime_value >= 500 then 'High Value'
+        when lifetime_value >= 100 then 'Medium Value'
+        when lifetime_value > 0 then 'Low Value'
+        else 'No Value'
+    end as value_segment
+from final

--- /dev/null
+++ b/models/marts/customer/customer_ltv.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,131 @@
+{{
+    config(
+        materialized='table',
+        tags=['marts', 'customers', 'ltv']
+    )
+}}
+
+/*
+================================================================================
+customer_ltv - corrected customer lifetime value (one row per customer)
+
+Why the previous LTV was overstated (see int_customers__lifetime_metrics):
+  1. Duplicate order lines: the same order line is loaded from both SAP and POS
+     (and sometimes more than once per system) in fct_sales. The old calculation
+     summed every copy, multiplying revenue.
+  2. Cancelled orders were counted: is_cancelled is derived only from
+     cancelled_at, but ~1,000 lines have order_status = 'CANCELLED' with no
+     cancelled_at. Those lines were still summed as revenue.
+
+Rules applied here:
+  - Normalize keys (trim / upper on order_id) and collapse copies to one row per
+    (order_id, line_number).
+  - A line is treated as cancelled if ANY copy has order_status 'CANCELLED',
+    is_cancelled = true, or cancelled_at set. Status code 'C' is NOT treated as
+    cancelled: those lines are fulfilled and shipped (SAP "completed" code).
+  - Lines with no customer_id on every copy are excluded.
+  - Customers with no valid orders are kept with zero values.
+
+Upstream staging models are not modified.
+================================================================================
+*/
+
+with order_lines as (
+
+    select
+        upper(trim(order_id))                                   as order_key,
+        line_number,
+        max(nullif(trim(customer_id), ''))                      as customer_id,
+        max(line_total)                                         as line_total,
+        bool_or(
+            upper(trim(order_status)) = 'CANCELLED'
+            or is_cancelled
+            or cancelled_at is not null
+        )                                                       as is_cancelled
+    from {{ ref('fct_sales') }}
+    group by 1, 2
+
+),
+
+-- Order date is order-level: many lines have a null order_date, but the same
+-- order usually has a dated sibling line. Use the order's date from any line.
+order_dates as (
+
+    select
+        upper(trim(order_id))                                   as order_key,
+        min(order_date)                                         as order_date
+    from {{ ref('fct_sales') }}
+    where order_date is not null
+    group by 1
+
+),
+
+valid_lines as (
+
+    select
+        l.order_key,
+        l.customer_id,
+        l.line_total,
+        d.order_date
+    from order_lines l
+    left join order_dates d
+        on d.order_key = l.order_key
+    where not l.is_cancelled
+      and l.customer_id is not null
+
+),
+
+customer_metrics as (
+
+    select
+        customer_id,
+        count(distinct order_key)                               as total_orders,
+        sum(line_total)                                         as lifetime_value,
+        min(order_date)                                         as first_order_date,
+        max(order_date)                                         as last_order_date
+    from valid_lines
+    group by customer_id
+
+),
+
+all_customers as (
+
+    select distinct customer_id
+    from {{ ref('dim_customers') }}
+    where customer_id is not null
+
+),
+
+customer_base as (
+
+    select
+        c.customer_id,
+        coalesce(m.total_orders, 0)                             as total_orders,
+        round(coalesce(m.lifetime_value, 0), 2)                 as lifetime_value,
+        m.first_order_date,
+        m.last_order_date
+    from all_customers c
+    left join customer_metrics m
+        on m.customer_id = c.customer_id
+
+)
+
+select
+    customer_id,
+    total_orders::integer                                       as total_orders,
+    lifetime_value::decimal(18, 2)                              as lifetime_value,
+    case
+        when total_orders > 0
+        then round(lifetime_value / total_orders, 2)
+        else 0
+    end::decimal(18, 2)                                         as avg_order_value,
+    first_order_date::date                                      as first_order_date,
+    last_order_date::date                                       as last_order_date,
+    case
+        when lifetime_value >= 1000 then 'VIP'
+        when lifetime_value >= 500  then 'High Value'
+        when lifetime_value >= 100  then 'Medium Value'
+        when lifetime_value > 0     then 'Low Value'
+        else 'No Value'
+    end::varchar                                                as value_segment
+from customer_base
